public.text: Definition of singular, multiple or complex nature of each of the 5 components decribed should be elaborated
public.suggestedRevision:
Client and facility registries are singular entities (even if they might be split/federated). The Facilities might also fall under different national systems (for example in the UK this might under Companies house for a private provider though this would need CH to become more sophisticated to be part of the generic DPI). A commercial registry (like CH) would itself be dependent on a person ID (generic DPI) and be prerequisite for the product registry (which would also need to cope with non-commercial sources of "product").
Workforce will likely fall mostly under professional regulators as the logical single controlling entity again a generic if health industry specific one for health professionals and needing something to cover other staff for other purposes (direct care and otherwise)
The life long health record as described is a complex entity that would be worthy of its own equivalent architectural description as it (defined for individual direct care) should be the central component of the DPI-H served by the others and as elsewhere recommended the priority of an ideal architecture (over secondary use cases).
Some of this is touched on in 652-659 but could do with broader exposition
